title: Pluggable Logging
hints: `MultiLogger` is itself an `ILogger` that holds `std::vector<ILogger*>` and forwards each call. Code that logs never knows whether it is talking to one logger or many: that is the Composite pattern.
requirements: `ConsoleLogger`, `MemoryLogger` (keeps the lines in a vector, handy for tests) and `NullLogger`
A `MultiLogger` that sends each line to several loggers
Filtering by level: below the chosen level, nothing is logged
A small class from an earlier project that receives an `ILogger&` in its constructor and logs what it does
stretch: A `TimestampLogger` that wraps another logger and puts the time in front of each line (the Decorator pattern), and a `FileLogger`.
